title: Why You Automatically Look Where Someone Else Looks
hook: Your eyes betray you, drawn by an invisible social string.

narration.text: When someone looks in a certain direction, your gaze will often follow automatically.
This is a primal, unconscious social cue, deeply wired into our brains.
Our brains contain specialised neurons that respond to eye gaze.
They create an immediate, involuntary shift in our attention.
It helps us quickly assess potential threats or opportunities in the environment.
You can feel this pull when someone glances away, even subtly.
Try it right now, then comment if it worked on you, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Ever wondered why your eyes follow someone else's gaze without you even trying? This short explains the automatic social cue that pulls your attention. It's a fascinating glimpse into how our brains are wired for social interaction and environmental awareness.
topic: Why you tend to look in the direction someone else is looking. This is an automatic social cue.
